newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi sees slow but steady Venezuela return.

text.p: Soft drinks giant PepsiCo will regain its footing in the Venezuelan market slowly but steadily, Pepsi Chief Executive Roger Enrico said Monday.

Pepsi was effectively ousted from the Venezuelan market in August when the country's leading bottler Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela broke a franchise agreement with the company to enter a joint venture with arch rival Coca-Cola Co.
"It's going to take us a good two years to get back to where we were," Enrico told reporters. "But let me tell you, this will not be a 100-yard dash ... we're here for a long time".

Pepsi -- which signed a 30/70 joint venture deal with leading Venezuelan foods and beverage company Polar in November to bottle and distribute cola -- expects sales to recover to 50 million cases by mid-1997 in a market estimated at 200 million cases a year.
Enrico also said PepsiCo had sold worldwide 1,000 company-owned restaurants to franchisees over the past year and a half and that it would continue that policy as franchisees were more efficient.
PepsiCo's stock rose 37.5 cents to $29.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
